chunks: From it, in the description of Faith: A path that is the brightest of courses, the most luminous of lamps,
for through Faith one is guided to virtuous actions, and through virtuous actions one is guided to Faith,
and through Faith knowledge is enriched, and through knowledge death is feared,
and through death this world is concluded, and through this world the Hereafter is secured,
and through Resurrection Paradise is brought near, and [as God said:] 'Hellfire is brought out for the deviators.'
and indeed the creation have no escape from Resurrection, traveling in its track towards the ultimate end.
ai.seo_question: How do faith and good deeds mutually reinforce each other according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) establishes a dialectical link between Iman and Amal, emphasizing that true faith is validated by righteous deeds and that knowledge, when rooted in faith, cultivates *war'* (awe of God) which mitigates the fear of death. This spiritual progression underscores the Shia emphasis on the unity of belief and action, where securing the Hereafter requires transcending worldly attachments through conscious mortality. The reference to Hell being 'revealed' (*tubarrazat*) for the misguided highlights the eschatological consequence of straying from this path of enlightened faith.

en.sayed-ali-raza: [A part of the same sermon :] This path is the lightest course and the brightest lamp.
Guidance towards virtuous actions is sought through faith while guidance towards faith is achieved through virtuous actions.
Knowledge is made to prosper through faith, and death is feared because of knowledge.
This world comes to an end with death, while the next world is secured (by virtuous actions) in this world.
For people there is no escape from resurrection. They are heading for this last end in its appointed course.
